lyrics:
[Spoken Word]

One Thousand and One Kayfabe Nights: the Arabian Nights as a wrestling show, where a boring story gets you killed.

Tonight I read you a deck of wrestling cards in order, one card per line.

The streaming bosses check whether you're still watching. King Shahryār checked too, holding an axe.

Kayfabe means everyone swears the fight is real. The Manifesto puts it plainer: History is a Work, Folklore is a Shoot.

Shahryār, the Destroyer, the heel promoter, thinks the roster is disposable. He's wrong.

Scheherazade, the Unending: she's turning the shoot into a work to save the locker room.

Dunyazad, the Hype Woman, keeps the heat alive: Sister, tell him the one about the apples!

Their father: The Grand Vizier, manager turned ref, caught between Bull and Fox; just following orders.

Aladdin, a rookie formerly working dark matches in a cave, now in the Main Event.

The African Sorcerer scouted the talent, only to get screwed out of the commission.

What he came for: The Wonderful Lamp, sentient brass, the ultimate Foreign Object; three wishes, No DQ.

Princess Badroulbadour wants the guy with the blue giant in his corner, not the Vizier's son.

No genie for him: Sinbad the Sailor, seven voyages, seven stipulations; bumps like a maniac, kicks out.

The Island-Whale, a sentient arena that No-Sells the fire; good luck selling this to the crowd.

The Giant Roc, the ultimate vertical suplex machine; takes you to the clouds, no landing pad.

The Roc drops him: The Diamond Valley, high risk, high reward; the floor is literally knives and snakes.

Worse than knives: The Giant, a tusked boar with a club; his Squash Match instantly destroys his Jobbers.

The Old Man of the Sea, a toad-grandpa backpack you can't take off: tap out or black out.

Sinbad pours: The Gourd of Wine, a Foreign Object used to break the submission hold; the Old Man sleeps.

The Shipwreck: the tour bus crashed, everyone starts from zero; shattered timbers on the shore.

Who starts from zero? Ali Baba, a woodcutter who found the master script, taxing the gold and the push.

Morgiana marked your coffins; the dance ends when the dagger hits, a ferret twirling daggers.

The greedy brother: Cassim forgot his lines, trapped in the cage with forty monsters behind a boulder.

The Magic Cave, the ultimate gated community: no one enters or leaves without the voice.

The cave's landlord: The Captain of Thieves, not here for gold, here for the Heat; a wolf howling orders.

The Thirty-Nine Grunts, individually weak, collectively a burial squad; a rat mob in motion.

The Marked Door: they tried to mark the house, but Morgiana marked the whole block.

Their plan B: The Oil Jar, hiding in the props department, a fatal mistake; a glowing eye inside.

Nobody bribes him: The King of Brass, clockwork lion, his contract written in rust; cannot be rewritten.

The Brass Horseman doesn't care about your story. He points to the grave with a bronze spear.

In that grave: The Mummified Queen, silent-era top draw; her promotion is dead, but she's still booking.

The Seven Tablets, stacked stone tablets with runes: read the spoilers, then leave the city.

Scheherazade invented the cliffhanger to dodge an axe. Now streaming bosses use it on us, and we're still watching.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!
lyrics2:
[Spoken Word]

One Thousand and One Kayfabe Nights, part two: in wrestling and in Baghdad, the better storyteller lives.

I'm your narrator; tonight we play Scheherazade and keep a killer king listening.

Think your job is shaky? Her husband fired a wife every morning, permanently.

Her whole career plan: stop at the good part.

Wrestling nerds, watch for the ref bump and the botched finish; book nerds, count the three apples.

Kayfabe, overdone: The Petrified Market, believed the story so much they became the set, a dead crowd.

Solomon's Vessel, original promoter's trap; even big guys can't break this contract.

Cork popped: The Howling Efreet, loudmouth on mic, screaming promos for centuries, sonic attack.

The Tower Lure, don't look down; height is a work, fall is a shoot, suicide dive.

Loves the height: Prince Qamar, mastered the screws; can't hit what you can't reach, aerial assault.

The Ebony Horse, mechanical work looks like magic; brass-saddled black horse with cogs.

Horse maker's grudge: The Indian Sage, heel inventor, he built the trap; you're just a kid in his saddle.

Sage's prize: Princess of Bengal, not crazy; cutting the best promo of her life to avoid the stable.

Abu Hasan, one night of wind, ten years of shame; footnote in a mother's calendar.

The Great Fart, biological accident as damaging as a steel chair; cheap heat for opponent.

Cheaper still, a corpse: The Hunchback, prop body, opossum jester slumped in red; Tag! You're the killer.

The Fishbone, tiny foreign object, ultimate no-sell; choking hazard, temporary death.

Dumped on his stairs: The Jewish Physician, tripped in the dark; this isn't medical school, it's a crime scene.

The Tailor, wanted to fix the body so no one would notice; stitching the squash.

The Steward, thought corpse was burglar, worked himself into a shoot; drunken brawl.

The Barber, the talker, saves the day by annoying everyone to death; filibuster.

Lion in rags: Harun al-Rashid, commissioner wanders streets to catch you breaking rules; audit.

Ja'far al-Barmaki, grand vizier cleans up Caliph's mess; enforcer destroys corruption.

Abu Nuwas, promo writer; segments legendary if he shows up sober, witty verse boosts faces.

Verse flops? Masrur the Executioner, when he steps in, the storyline ends; the bell, if King orders it.

Three days: The Locked Chest, don't open it; the smell isn't gold, it's a botched finish, dead wait.

The Missing Apple, one apple for a life, a fair trade in a nonsensical world, clue.

The Jealous Husband, saw the apple and saw red; no one gets a happy ending, rage.

The Slave, took the apple, took the heat, scapegoat; damage intended for another.

Suspension of Disbelief, currency of the realm; keep marks believing, Bizarro sell.

Losing the marks? The Montreal Screwjob, massive heat, unfair reset; the boss wins, ref grabbing belt.

Against Masrur: The Cliffhanger, the only defense against the Executioner; to be continued next night.

Kayfabizarro Mask, to lose the mask is to lose your soul; keep it on, true face, no reveals.

Scheherazade told stories to stay alive; today's promoters tell them to stay rich.

She bought another morning. We buy season two.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!
